title: Fish Hatchery Management
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned Nigerian university 300L Fish Hatchery Management curriculum: broodstock selection and conditioning, induced breeding techniques (hypophysation, hormone use), spawning, egg fertilization and incubation, hatching, larval and fry rearing, nursery management, and hatchery facility design/water quality control -- centered on Clarias (catfish) and Oreochromis (tilapia), the dominant species in Nigerian hatchery practice.

questions.question: Broodstock in fish hatchery management refers to:
options: Sexually mature fish maintained and selected specifically for breeding purposes
Juvenile fish recently hatched from eggs
Fish reared exclusively for the food market
Wild fish caught for immediate consumption
questions.correct_answer: Sexually mature fish maintained and selected specifically for breeding purposes
questions.explanation: Broodstock are mature, healthy fish selected and conditioned specifically to produce eggs and milt for propagation.

questions.question: Which characteristic is most important when selecting broodfish for induced breeding?
options: Good health, appropriate age/size, and clear secondary sexual characteristics indicating readiness to spawn
The fish's market weight at the time of harvest
The color pattern of the fish's scales
The fish's swimming speed in the pond
questions.correct_answer: Good health, appropriate age/size, and clear secondary sexual characteristics indicating readiness to spawn
questions.explanation: Good broodstock selection targets healthy, disease-free fish of suitable maturity with visible signs of breeding readiness, such as a swollen, reddish genital papilla in females.

questions.question: In female Clarias gariepinus (catfish) broodstock, a key external sign of readiness for induced spawning is:
options: A swollen, soft, and reddish genital (urogenital) papilla
A noticeably smaller body size than males
Dull, pale skin coloration
A rigid, flattened abdomen
questions.correct_answer: A swollen, soft, and reddish genital (urogenital) papilla
questions.explanation: Ripe female catfish typically show a swollen, soft, reddish genital papilla and a distended, soft abdomen full of eggs, indicating readiness for hormone-induced spawning.

questions.question: Induced breeding (hypophysation) in fish hatchery practice involves:
options: Administering hormones to stimulate final maturation and ovulation/spermiation in broodfish that do not spawn naturally in captivity
Physically massaging fish to extract eggs without any hormonal treatment
Feeding broodfish a special high-protein diet to trigger spawning
Exposing fish to bright light for extended photoperiods only
questions.correct_answer: Administering hormones to stimulate final maturation and ovulation/spermiation in broodfish that do not spawn naturally in captivity
questions.explanation: Induced breeding uses hormone injections (e.g., pituitary extract, HCG, or synthetic analogues) to trigger the hormonal cascade needed for ovulation and milt release in species that resist natural spawning in confinement.

questions.question: Which of the following is a commonly used hormone preparation in induced spawning of catfish?
options: Ovaprim (a synthetic GnRH analogue with dopamine antagonist)
Insulin
Penicillin
Ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA)
questions.correct_answer: Ovaprim (a synthetic GnRH analogue with dopamine antagonist)
questions.explanation: Ovaprim is a widely used commercial hormone preparation that stimulates the release of gonadotropin to induce ovulation and spermiation in catfish and other species.

questions.question: Crude carp pituitary extract is used in induced fish breeding because it contains:
options: Gonadotropic hormones that stimulate final gonadal maturation and spawning
Digestive enzymes that improve feed conversion
Antibiotics that prevent disease in hatchlings
Vitamins that accelerate juvenile growth
questions.correct_answer: Gonadotropic hormones that stimulate final gonadal maturation and spawning
questions.explanation: Fish pituitary glands are rich in gonadotropins; extracts from donor fish (often carp) are injected to trigger maturation and spawning in recipient broodfish.

questions.question: The technique of manually expelling eggs from a ripe female fish by applying gentle pressure to the abdomen is called:
options: Stripping
Grading
Fertilization
Acclimation
questions.correct_answer: Stripping
questions.explanation: Stripping is the manual expression of eggs (and, for males, milt) by applying gentle pressure along the abdomen toward the genital opening.

questions.question: In artificial (dry) fertilization of catfish eggs, why are eggs and milt typically mixed in a dry container before water is added?
options: Sperm become activated and motile upon contact with water, so mixing dry first maximizes the chance of fertilization before motility is lost
It prevents the eggs from absorbing any water at all
It is required to change the color of the eggs
It reduces the total number of eggs produced
questions.correct_answer: Sperm become activated and motile upon contact with water, so mixing dry first maximizes the chance of fertilization before motility is lost
questions.explanation: Fish sperm are typically immotile until activated by water; dry mixing ensures milt and eggs are in close contact so fertilization occurs efficiently once water activates the sperm, since motility is brief.

questions.question: Milt, as used in hatchery terminology, refers to:
options: The seminal fluid containing sperm released by male fish
The mature eggs released by female fish
A type of larval feed
The mucus coating on fish eggs
questions.correct_answer: The seminal fluid containing sperm released by male fish
questions.explanation: Milt is the fish equivalent of semen, the fluid containing sperm that males release to fertilize eggs.

questions.question: In hatchery practice, why must the testes of a sacrificed male catfish sometimes be macerated to obtain milt?
options: Because catfish males may not release sufficient milt by simple pressure, so the testes are removed and crushed in a diluent to release sperm
Because it improves the color of the resulting fry
Because it is required by law in all hatcheries
Because macerated testes fertilize eggs faster than intact milt
questions.correct_answer: Because catfish males may not release sufficient milt by simple pressure, so the testes are removed and crushed in a diluent to release sperm
questions.explanation: Unlike some species, male catfish often yield little milt by stripping, so hatchery operators sacrifice the male, remove the testes, and macerate them in a saline diluent to obtain adequate sperm for fertilizing a batch of eggs.

questions.question: Egg incubation in a hatchery is best described as the period during which:
options: Fertilized eggs are held under controlled conditions until they hatch into larvae
Broodfish are conditioned before spawning
Fry are transported from the hatchery to grow-out ponds
Feed is formulated for juvenile fish
questions.correct_answer: Fertilized eggs are held under controlled conditions until they hatch into larvae
questions.explanation: Incubation is the stage from fertilization to hatching, during which eggs develop under suitable water quality, temperature, and oxygen conditions.

questions.question: Which water quality factor most directly influences the rate of embryonic development and hatching time in fish eggs?
options: Water temperature
Water color
Pond surface area
Distance from the hatchery building
questions.correct_answer: Water temperature
questions.explanation: Temperature strongly governs the metabolic rate of developing embryos; warmer water (within tolerable limits) speeds development and shortens time to hatching.

questions.question: Adhesive fish eggs, such as those of catfish, are often spread on which substrate during incubation to prevent clumping and fungal infection?
options: A spawning mat, kakaban, or similar mesh/fibrous substrate
A metal tray with no water flow
Dry sand
A layer of pond mud
questions.correct_answer: A spawning mat, kakaban, or similar mesh/fibrous substrate
questions.explanation: Adhesive eggs are spread thinly on fibrous mats (kakaban) or mesh screens so they don't clump together, which reduces fungal growth and improves water circulation and oxygen supply around each egg.

questions.question: Fungal infection (e.g., Saprolegnia) of incubating fish eggs is commonly managed in hatcheries by:
options: Treating eggs with a mild disinfectant such as malachite green or methylene blue and removing dead/infected eggs
Increasing water temperature to boiling point
Completely removing all water from the incubator
Feeding the eggs a protein-rich diet
questions.correct_answer: Treating eggs with a mild disinfectant such as malachite green or methylene blue and removing dead/infected eggs
questions.explanation: Fungal growth on dead or unfertilized eggs can spread to healthy eggs; hatchery managers use mild fungicidal treatments and remove affected eggs to limit spread.

questions.question: The newly hatched fish, before it begins external feeding and is still nourished by its yolk sac, is termed:
options: A larva (yolk-sac larva)
A fingerling
A juvenile
A broodfish
questions.correct_answer: A larva (yolk-sac larva)
questions.explanation: Immediately after hatching, the fish is a larva that relies on its attached yolk sac for nutrition before it develops the ability to feed externally.

questions.question: Why is the timing of first exogenous (external) feeding critical in larval fish rearing?
options: Larvae must begin external feeding soon after yolk sac absorption is complete, or they will starve and suffer high mortality
External feeding has no effect on larval survival
Larvae never need external feed if raised in green water
First feeding timing only affects the coloration of adult fish
questions.correct_answer: Larvae must begin external feeding soon after yolk sac absorption is complete, or they will starve and suffer high mortality
questions.explanation: There is a critical window ('point of no return') after yolk reserves are depleted; if larvae fail to find suitable food in time, they weaken and die, so timely provision of appropriate first feed is essential.

questions.question: Which live feed is commonly used as a first food for catfish and tilapia larvae in hatcheries?
options: Artemia nauplii (brine shrimp) or Moina/Daphnia
Whole maize grains
Wheat bran
Adult earthworms
questions.correct_answer: Artemia nauplii (brine shrimp) or Moina/Daphnia
questions.explanation: Small live zooplankton such as newly hatched Artemia nauplii or Moina/Daphnia are appropriately sized, nutritious first foods that closely match the small mouth gape of fish larvae.

questions.question: Cannibalism is a major challenge in the larval and fry stage of which commonly hatchery-produced Nigerian species in particular?
options: Clarias gariepinus (African catfish)
Oreochromis niloticus (Nile tilapia) exclusively
Common carp exclusively
None of the commonly farmed species show cannibalism
questions.correct_answer: Clarias gariepinus (African catfish)
questions.explanation: Catfish fry are notoriously cannibalistic due to size variation and aggressive feeding behavior, requiring frequent grading and adequate feeding to reduce losses.

questions.question: Grading of fry and fingerlings during nursery rearing is done primarily to:
options: Sort fish by size to reduce size-related aggression/cannibalism and promote uniform growth
Separate male fish from female fish
Determine the exact age of each fish
Prepare fish for hormonal sex reversal
questions.correct_answer: Sort fish by size to reduce size-related aggression/cannibalism and promote uniform growth
questions.explanation: Grading separates fish into size classes, reducing cannibalism of smaller individuals by larger ones and allowing more uniform feeding and growth within each group.

questions.question: A nursery pond, as distinct from a grow-out pond, is used mainly to:
options: Rear fry into fingerlings under closely managed conditions before stocking into larger grow-out systems
House only broodstock throughout their reproductive life
Store harvested market-size fish before sale
Treat sick adult fish
questions.correct_answer: Rear fry into fingerlings under closely managed conditions before stocking into larger grow-out systems
questions.explanation: Nursery ponds/tanks provide a protected, closely monitored intermediate stage where delicate fry grow into hardier fingerlings before being moved to grow-out ponds.

questions.question: Hatchery water for egg incubation and larval rearing should ideally be:
options: Clean, well-oxygenated, and free of chlorine and other toxicants
High in chlorine to sterilize the eggs
As turbid and muddy as possible
Completely devoid of dissolved oxygen
questions.correct_answer: Clean, well-oxygenated, and free of chlorine and other toxicants
questions.explanation: Eggs and larvae are highly sensitive to poor water quality; hatchery water must be clean, adequately oxygenated, and free of chlorine, heavy metals, or other toxic substances.

questions.question: In a recirculating hatchery system, the biofilter's main function is to:
options: Convert toxic ammonia excreted by fish into less harmful nitrite and then nitrate via nitrifying bacteria
Add color to the water for aesthetic purposes
Increase the water's salinity
Physically remove eggs from the incubation trough
questions.correct_answer: Convert toxic ammonia excreted by fish into less harmful nitrite and then nitrate via nitrifying bacteria
questions.explanation: Biofilters host nitrifying bacteria that carry out nitrification, converting toxic ammonia to nitrite and then to the much less toxic nitrate, maintaining safe water quality in recirculating systems.

questions.question: Which of these is an essential structural component of a typical fish hatchery facility?
options: A reliable water supply and reservoir system with pumps and filtration
A large parking lot for staff vehicles
A retail shop selling processed fish
An office exclusively for accounting staff
questions.correct_answer: A reliable water supply and reservoir system with pumps and filtration
questions.explanation: A dependable, high-quality water supply is fundamental to hatchery operation, since all breeding, incubation, and larval rearing depend on continuous clean water.

questions.question: Hapa nets, as used in tilapia hatchery operations, are best described as:
options: Fine-mesh net enclosures suspended in ponds used for breeding, egg/fry collection, or nursing
Large trawl nets used in marine capture fisheries
Solid concrete tanks used for broodstock holding
Filters used to remove sediment from hatchery water
questions.correct_answer: Fine-mesh net enclosures suspended in ponds used for breeding, egg/fry collection, or nursing
questions.explanation: Hapas are mesh net enclosures set within a pond, widely used in tilapia hatchery operations to confine breeding pairs or nurse fry under controlled, observable conditions.

questions.question: Tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus), unlike catfish, naturally practices which reproductive behavior that hatchery managers can exploit without hormone injection?
options: Mouth-brooding of fertilized eggs by the female
External fertilization in open water with no parental care
Laying eggs exclusively on land
Producing live young rather than eggs
questions.correct_answer: Mouth-brooding of fertilized eggs by the female
questions.explanation: Female Nile tilapia are maternal mouth-brooders, incubating fertilized eggs and guarding fry in their mouths, a natural behavior hatchery operators use to collect eggs/fry without hormone-induced spawning.

questions.question: Sex reversal in tilapia hatchery production, typically achieved by feeding fry a hormone (e.g., 17-alpha-methyltestosterone), is done to:
options: Produce mostly male populations, since males grow faster and this avoids uncontrolled breeding in grow-out ponds
Increase the number of eggs a female tilapia can produce
Change the color of tilapia to make them more marketable
Eliminate the need for hatchery water quality management
questions.correct_answer: Produce mostly male populations, since males grow faster and this avoids uncontrolled breeding in grow-out ponds
questions.explanation: Because male tilapia grow faster than females and uncontrolled breeding in grow-out ponds leads to stunted overpopulation, hatcheries commonly sex-reverse fry to all-male populations using hormone-treated feed during a critical early developmental window.

questions.question: The stocking density of fry in nursery tanks or hapas should be carefully controlled mainly because overcrowding:
options: Leads to poor water quality, increased stress, disease, and slower or uneven growth
Has no effect on fry survival or growth
Always improves feed conversion efficiency
Automatically increases the sex ratio toward females
questions.correct_answer: Leads to poor water quality, increased stress, disease, and slower or uneven growth
questions.explanation: High stocking density increases waste accumulation and competition for oxygen and food, degrading water quality and fish welfare, which reduces growth and survival.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes 'weaning' in hatchery fry management?
options: The gradual transition of fry from live feed to formulated (artificial) diets
The process of separating male and female broodstock
The removal of unfertilized eggs from the incubator
The transport of fingerlings from hatchery to farm
questions.correct_answer: The gradual transition of fry from live feed to formulated (artificial) diets
questions.explanation: Weaning refers to gradually shifting fry nutrition from live feed (which mimics natural prey) to manufactured feed, a critical and sometimes delicate stage in hatchery production.

questions.question: Hatching rate (hatchability) in a hatchery batch is calculated as:
options: The number of eggs that successfully hatch expressed as a percentage of the total number of fertilized eggs incubated
The total weight of fish produced divided by the pond area
The number of broodfish used divided by the number of technicians on duty
The number of days from fertilization to first feeding
questions.correct_answer: The number of eggs that successfully hatch expressed as a percentage of the total number of fertilized eggs incubated
questions.explanation: Hatchability is a key hatchery performance indicator, calculated as the proportion of incubated fertilized eggs that successfully hatch into larvae.

questions.question: Transporting live fingerlings from a hatchery to a farm over long distances typically requires:
options: Oxygenated water in sealed containers or bags, often with reduced temperature to lower metabolic rate and stress
Complete removal of water from the transport container
Direct sunlight exposure throughout transport to keep fish warm
Feeding fish heavily just before loading them for transport
questions.correct_answer: Oxygenated water in sealed containers or bags, often with reduced temperature to lower metabolic rate and stress
questions.explanation: Successful live fish transport depends on adequate dissolved oxygen (often supplemented), and usually reduced temperature to slow metabolism and minimize stress and mortality en route; fish are typically starved briefly before transport to reduce waste output.

questions.question: Latency period, in the context of hormone-induced spawning, refers to:
options: The time interval between hormone injection and ovulation/stripping readiness in the female
The time a fish egg takes to fully decompose
The lifespan of a broodfish after its final spawning
The period a hatchery remains closed between breeding seasons
questions.correct_answer: The time interval between hormone injection and ovulation/stripping readiness in the female
questions.explanation: Latency period is the hormone-to-ovulation interval, which varies with species, hormone dose, and water temperature, and determines when the female should be stripped.
